us: Trump: 'semi-negotiating' chess game · Caine off-ramp report
effects: Tally 55/2/2 · Jazan refinery ablaze again · Transits down to six
tldr: Trump described a deliberate economic squeeze — 'low-keying it,' only 'semi-negotiating' — as CNN reported the Joint Chiefs chairman privately telling advisers the US needed an off-ramp. Tehran insisted intermediary messages were not talks and demanded compensation first. Tenth consecutive night without confirmed strikes inside Iran.

events.title: Trump frames the standoff as an economic chess game
events.summary: To Axios: the US is 'low-keying it' with Iran, 'semi-negotiating.' His argument was Iran's balance sheet — 'huge inflation and the fact they have no money,' troops struggling to be paid, oil just above $75. Separately, CNN reported Joint Chiefs chairman General Dan Caine had privately told other advisers the remaining escalation options could backfire and the US needed a way out.

events.title: Araghchi: messages through intermediaries are not negotiations
events.summary: 'The process should not be called negotiations' — talks cannot resume until Washington compensates for breaching the June memorandum. Pezeshkian voiced hope the Oman talks would deliver.

events.title: Drone sets Jazan refinery alight again; al-Makha deaths mount
events.summary: Yahya Saree claimed a direct drone hit on Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery — shut since July 27; fire extinguished, no injuries. Houthi missile attacks on Yemen's al-Makha port on August 9 killed at least 11 (eight soldiers, three civilians) and wounded 32.
